shill: Fix bogus warnings in UpdateFromIPConfig on IPv6-only networks If a network is IPv6-only, or if the IPv6 configuration occurs before the DHCPv4 configuration, Connection::UpdateFromIPConfig() will be run against |Device::ip6config_| instead of |Device::ipconfig_|. This does not happen on normal mixed IPv4+IPv6 networks so it is somewhat of a corner case. UpdateFromIPConfig() makes two assumptions that are only valid on IPv4: 1) That a broadcast address exists. IPv6 only uses multicast. 2) That the default gateway will have the same prefix as our global scope address. On IPv6 the gateway address is typically a link-local address. Disable these two warnings for IPv6. BUG=chromium:727242 TEST=manually hack device.cc to delay IPv4 address assignment, then check the logs to see what happens when UpdateFromIPConfig() is run on an IPv6 configuration TEST=unit tests Change-Id: Id343e49f363ab5efaa5be0987a3f138d6279a4ec Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/580642 Commit-Ready: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org> Tested-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org>

shill: Make the default Connection::metric_ work on IPv6 The kernel's IPv4 implementation allows routes with metric 0 to be created, but the kernel's IPv6 implementation changes metric 0 routes to metric 1024. This causes shill's route cache to get out of sync with the running kernel, causing the default IPv6 route to be unexpectedly deleted under some circumstances. Fix this by defaulting to kNonDefaultMetricBase (10) instead of 0. BUG=chromium:727242 TEST=manually hack device.cc to delay IPv4 address assignment, then check the logs to see what happens when UpdateFromIPConfig() is run on an IPv6 configuration TEST=unit tests Change-Id: Iac4d6ef3a881f2820a4ef4dd3fdda6475937d5f9 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/580643 Commit-Ready: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org> Tested-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org>

cbuildbot: Clean up loopback-based chroots If the loopback device file isn't deleted when cleaning up the chroot, the next cros_sdk run will attempt to re-mount the same image if it supports loopback chroots. Since the builders do their cleanup after a reboot, they will end up deleting the empty directory and then re-mounting the previously populated chroot. This CL should keep the buildbots clean when they start processing crrev.com/c/553462 until the loopback chroot support is fully landed. power: Don't suspend console when using suspend_to_idle Suspend_on_idle on Intel systems is intended to take the system into a low power state S0ix instead of S3. Intel identified that not suspending the UART can cause failure to go into S0ix state (via suspend-to-idle) and thus rendering system stay in higher package power state such as PC10, because a non suspended UART can cause events that affect PMC's decision to enter S0ix. Hence this patch suspends the console when using Suspend-to- idle. The suspend and resume kernel logs are still going to be available in dmesg / syslog. The logs will also eventually appear on the UART itself (but will be printed after a delay because the messages are saved in a buffer and printed after the UART is resumed). BUG=b:63737106 TEST=check that console is suspended when using S0ix, and not suspended when using S3. Change-Id: I5b0b28e5e19fe181fa6e58ad67b2f443934b8832 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/580674 Commit-Ready: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Rajneesh Bhardwaj <rajneesh.bhardwaj@intel.com>
